newsitem.title: JAMAICA: Jamaica says U.S. agrees to regional gun talks.
newsitem.headline: Jamaica says U.S. agrees to regional gun talks.

text.p: Jamaica said on Thursday that Washington had agreed to participate in regional gun smuggling talks, following Jamaica's request for talks to stop the weapons trade.

In a news release, Jamaican officials said President Bill Clinton's approval was conveyed in a letter to Jamaican Prime Minister P.J. Patterson on Wednesday by Richard Clarke, Clinton's special assistant for global issues.

Patterson had written earlier this month to his colleagues in the 14-member Caribbean Community (Caricom) and to the U.S. president proposing the talks to avoid the diplomatic dispute created when Caribbean countries negotiated separate drug interdiction agreements.

Known as "shiprider" agreements, the pacts allow U.S. agents to operate in the individual nations' territorial waters and airspace. And while most Caribbean states have signed on, Jamaica and Barbados have resisted, calling the pacts a violation of their sovereignty.
Jamaica also tried and failed to include talks on gun smuggling in the negotiations with Washington on the shiprider accord.
There were 920 murders in Jamaica in 1996, and Jamaican authorities contend most were committed with weapons believed to have been smuggled in from the United States.

Patterson has said he hopes the United States will sign the weapons agreement when Clinton travels to Barbados in May for a summit with leaders from the English-speaking Caribbean, Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
